title: FastGPT code sandbox -- T1059.007 block-comment regex bypass on dynamic import() reaches child_process
author: WinstonRedGuard -- sigma plugin observed rules (derived from breach corpus)
description:
Vendor-disclosed detection for CVE-2026-44287 (GHSA-f5mq-qxm4-5mvc), a
self-reported advisory for FastGPT, an AI Agent building platform.

Prior to 4.15.0-beta1, the JavaScript sandbox worker
(`projects/code-sandbox/src/pool/worker.ts:356`) blocks dynamic
`import()` with `/\bimport\s*\(/.test(code)`. The regex's `\s` class
matches only ASCII whitespace; a block comment
(`/* ... */`, whose delimiter bytes `/`, `*`, `*`, `/` are NOT in `\s`)
is valid JavaScript grammar between `import` and `(` but invisible to
the regex. The payload `import/**/("child_process")` therefore parses
as a syntactically valid dynamic import the filter never sees. Because
the sandbox's `safeRequire` Proxy wraps only `require()` -- not
`import()` -- the loaded `child_process` module is fully unrestricted,
and `execSync(...)` runs arbitrary commands as `uid=100(sandbox)` inside
the sandbox container. The advisory's own PoC: `const cp = await
import/**/("child_process"); cp.execSync("id")`.

Detection logic flags exactly the bypass idiom rather than a generic
"import used" heuristic: the literal sequence `import` immediately
followed by a `/*...*/`-style comment and then `(` -- a syntactically
odd construction with no ordinary reason to appear in submitted code
other than evading a whitespace-only filter.

Aggregated from 1 first-party vendor security advisory (labring, via
GHSA and NVD), fixed in 4.15.0-beta1.
